answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: James Joyce wrote this in episode 2, “Nestor,” of Ulysses (1922). Stephen Dedalus says it to Mr. Deasy; “Stephen said” is the narrator’s attribution, not part of Stephen’s spoken sentence.

author.name: James Joyce
author.heading: About James Joyce
author.bio: James Joyce transformed the representation of speech and thought in modern fiction. His works include Dubliners, A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man, Ulysses and Finnegans Wake, repeatedly returning to Dublin even while he lived abroad.

cite.pageCitation: Quotle.info. “Who really said ‘History, Stephen said, is a nightmare from which I am trying to awake’?” Last verified 9 Nov 2026.

copyAttribution: James Joyce, Ulysses (1922), episode 2, “Nestor”; Stephen Dedalus speaking to Mr. Deasy. “Stephen said” is the narrative attribution.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Stephen’s remark interrupts Mr. Deasy’s confident account of history, guilt and national identity. Deasy replies that history moves toward a divine goal, so the exchange places the nightmare image against an explicitly opposed interpretation within the novel.
